outcome: Not settled as of 13 October 2026. Since 26 January 2024 the only claimed resolution is a single-author, unaffiliated arXiv preprint (Gore, arXiv 2506.04299, June 2025) that I found no qualified engagement with; Tao and Yang (arXiv 2510.10151, October 2025) prove Markov's equation is not partition regular, which is a necessary condition for uniqueness and does not settle it; the other in-window items (Fisac 2025 reformulation, Chen and Jia 2025, Banaian 2025, Banaian and Huang 2026, Gyoda and Maruyama's 2026 journal publication of a 2023 preprint, Veselov 2026, Gyoda 2026 survey, O'Sullivan 2026) either treat generalised or neighbouring equations, reformulate the conjecture, or restate it as open; none has been checked by anyone I could find.
problem_asks: The statement asks, for the classical Markov Diophantine equation x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 3xyz over positive integers: (1) for every Markov number m (every positive integer occurring in a solution triple), (2) there is exactly one normalized solution (taken as a triple a <= b <= c) whose largest entry is m. Unpacked: (1a) existence, that m occurs as the largest entry of at least one normalized solution (presented in the sources I read as part of the standard tree theory, which I did not verify from a primary source); (1b) uniqueness, that at most one normalized solution has largest entry m, equivalently that a Markov triple is determined by its largest entry, equivalently that the Markov tree has no repeated numbers. The statement itself does not ask for a bound, an asymptotic, a finite check, or a generalisation to other equations; the constants 3 and the ordering convention are part of the question as stated. Frobenius posed it in 1913 (Wikipedia wording: 'the unicity conjecture, as remarked by Frobenius in 1913').

events.what_happened: Qing Zhou posted 'On the uniqueness conjecture for Markoff triples' (arXiv math/0010131), claiming to show that a Markoff triple is determined by its largest entry. The v2 of 3 Nov 2000 is a withdrawal: 'This paper has been withdrawn by author due to an error in the proof.' Opened the arXiv abstract page.
events.revisions: v1 13 Oct 2000 (557 KB, the claimed proof); v2 3 Nov 2000 (1 KB) withdrawn by author for an error in the proof.
events.delivers: Claimed: the full classical uniqueness statement (a Markoff triple is determined by its largest entry). The claim is withdrawn; the withdrawal says the proof has an error, and the v1 text is not in the abstract I read.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, as far as the withdrawn version is concerned.
events.doubts: The author withdrew it for an error in the proof. I did not read the v1 text, so I cannot say where the error lies.

withdrawn.what: The v1 claimed proof of uniqueness, withdrawn in v2.

events.direction: Claims uniqueness, i.e. in the direction of the conjecture as stated; withdrawn.

events.what_happened: Arthur Baragar, 'On the Unicity Conjecture for Markoff Numbers', Canadian Mathematical Bulletin 39(1) (1996) pp. 3-9. Shows the unicity property (for each Markoff number m, at most one pair x <= y <= m with x^2 + y^2 + m^2 = 3xym) for m such that m, 3m-2 or 3m+2 is prime, twice a prime or four times a prime. Opened the Cambridge page (published online 20 Nov 2018; the print issue is 1996).
events.delivers: Uniqueness for Markov numbers m satisfying the stated arithmetic conditions (m, 3m-2 or 3m+2 prime, twice a prime, or four times a prime). A restricted class of the classical statement.
events.remains: Uniqueness for all Markov numbers outside those classes; existence is not in question here.

checked_by.qualification: Peer-reviewed journal in which the paper appeared

events.direction: Proves uniqueness in a restricted class; the conjecture is not settled.

events.what_happened: J. O. Button, 'Markoff numbers, principal ideals and continued fraction expansions', Journal of Number Theory 87(1) (2001) 77-95. Shows the uniqueness holds 'in a range of cases' by factorisation of ideals in certain quadratic fields, and gives a counterexample to that approach when the question is widened to other numbers. Opened the Oxford ORA record of the paper.
events.delivers: Uniqueness in a range of cases (scope per the abstract; the paper's prime-power result is reported second-hand in later papers, which I did not check against the paper itself).
events.remains: Uniqueness for the remaining Markov numbers. The abstract also records a counterexample to the method for the wider question.

checked_by.who: Journal of Number Theory (Elsevier), editorial process

events.direction: Partial: uniqueness in a range of cases.

events.what_happened: Mong Lung Lang and Ser Peow Tan, 'A simple proof of the Markoff conjecture for prime powers', arXiv math/0508443 (24 Aug 2005), published Geometry & Dedicata 129 (2007) 15-22. Gives a proof of uniqueness when the largest entry c is a prime power, independent of Button and Schmutz. Opened the arXiv abstract page.
events.revisions: v1 only on arXiv; journal Geometriae Dedicata 129 (2007).
events.delivers: Uniqueness when the largest entry is a prime power. A restricted class.
events.remains: All other Markov numbers.

checked_by.who: Geometriae Dedicata (journal of record, per the arXiv journal reference)

events.direction: Partial: uniqueness for prime-power largest entries.

events.what_happened: Ying Zhang, 'An elementary proof of uniqueness of Markoff numbers which are prime powers', arXiv math/0606283 (v1 12 Jun 2006; v2 1 Feb 2007, 'thoroughly rewritten, title changed'). Gives uniqueness for Markoff numbers that are prime powers or twice prime powers, without algebraic number theory or hyperbolic geometry. Opened the arXiv abstract page.
events.delivers: Uniqueness for Markoff numbers that are prime powers or twice prime powers.
events.remains: All other Markov numbers.

events.what_happened: Ying Zhang, 'Congruence and Uniqueness of Certain Markoff Numbers', arXiv math/0612620 (20 Dec 2006; v2 29 Dec 2006), listed as Acta Arithmetica 128 (2007) 295-301. Shows every even Markoff number is 2 mod 32 and generalises a result of Baragar, giving uniqueness for Markoff numbers c where 3c-2 or 3c+2 is a prime power, 4 times a prime power, or 8 times a prime power. Opened the arXiv abstract page.
events.delivers: Uniqueness for Markoff numbers c with 3c-2 or 3c+2 a prime power, 4 times a prime power, or 8 times a prime power.
events.remains: All other Markov numbers.

checked_by.who: Acta Arithmetica (journal of record, per the arXiv journal reference)

events.what_happened: A claimed proof by Gerhard Rosenberger, 1976, reported in later sources as faulty. I did not open a primary source for this; it comes from search summaries that cited a minortriad.com page and the Wikipedia/Markov literature, so the venue and content are unverified.
events.delivers: Claimed proof of the classical uniqueness statement; reported as faulty by second-hand sources.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, if the claim is taken to be wrong.
events.doubts: Reported as faulty by second-hand sources only; I did not read the 1976 paper or the critique.

events.what_happened: Norbert Riedel, 'Markoff Equation and Nilpotent Matrices', arXiv 0709.1499, first posted 10 Sep 2007. Claims the largest member of a Markoff triple determines the other two, via upper triangular 3x3 matrices, presented as an answer to a question open almost 100 years. Withdrawn: v7 of 29 Mar 2013 'This paper has been withdrawn by Norbert Riedel'; the comments say most of the correct portion was incorporated into arXiv 1208.4032.
events.revisions: v1 10 Sep 2007; v2 13 Sep 2007; v3 4 Dec 2007; v4 5 Aug 2008; v5 12 Mar 2009; v6 28 Jul 2009; v7 29 Mar 2013 withdrawn.
events.delivers: Claimed: uniqueness of the other two members given the largest (the classical statement). Withdrawn; the withdrawal notice gives no reason.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, as far as this version is concerned.
events.doubts: A review of the 2007 approach (HAL record hal-00406601, 'From Frobenius to Riedel') reports 'deficiencies in his developments, showing that the conjecture still resists'. I could not open the HAL record (access blocked), so this rests on a search summary; I did not confirm the review's authors or date.

withdrawn.what: arXiv 0709.1499 (v7), withdrawn by the author; the correct portion said to be moved to arXiv 1208.4032.

events.what_happened: HAL record hal-00406601, 'From Frobenius to Riedel: analysis of the solutions of the Markoff equation', a review that checks Riedel's 2007 computations and reports deficiencies in them. I could not open it (access blocked by a bot-check page). What I have is a search summary of its abstract: it verifies Riedel's computations, gives corrections, and states the authors 'put in light some deficiency in his developments, showing that the conjecture still resists'.
events.delivers: Not a resolution; reports that the 2007 approach has gaps.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.

checked_by.who: Authors not confirmed (a search summary attributed the review to Ying Zhang's group, which I could not verify)
checked_by.what_they_did: Reviewed Riedel's 2007 computations and reported deficiencies

events.doubts: The year is inferred from the HAL identifier range and the search summary, not from the record itself, which I could not open. The review addresses the 2007 version, not the 2012 claim.
events.direction: Against the 2007 claim (reports gaps); the conjecture stays open per the review.

events.what_happened: Norbert Riedel, 'On the Markoff Equation', arXiv 1208.4032 (v1 20 Aug 2012; twelve versions, last 25 Aug 2022). Recasts the Markoff tree in integral upper unitriangular 3x3 matrices and claims that 'the largest member of such a triple determines the other two uniquely', adding 'This answers a question which has been open for 100 years.' Opened the arXiv abstract page and an ar5iv rendering (the ar5iv version number is not stated; it may predate v12).
events.delivers: Claimed: uniqueness (largest entry determines the triple), i.e. the classical statement, via prime ideal factorisation in quadratic fields and the paper's machinery on binary quadratic forms. Not refereed in any journal I could find.
events.remains: None if the claim is correct; the paper is the claimed full resolution.
events.doubts: (1) In the ar5iv rendering I read, after Proposition 4.6 the author writes that the framework cannot 'settle the uniqueness question' because the characterisation of alpha is too 'elusive'. (2) The rendering has matrix identities labelled '(incomplete)' with entries (2,1) and (2,2) marked open, and Lemma 5.7 is settled by case checking. The version in that rendering is not stated, so these may have been fixed in v12. (3) The 2007 precursor was withdrawn, and a 2007-2009 review found deficiencies in it. (4) Second-hand: Sondow's 2015 OEIS comment reports Sarnak saying all claims to prove the unicity conjecture have turned out to be false. I could not read v12 in full.
events.direction: Claims uniqueness, in the direction of the conjecture as stated.

events.what_happened: Matty van Son, 'Uniqueness conjectures for extended Markov numbers', arXiv 1911.00746 (2 Nov 2019). Defines extended uniqueness conjectures for arbitrary sequences and shows that the extended conjecture fails for mu=(a,a), nu=(b,b) for certain a>1, b>2. Opened the arXiv abstract page.
events.delivers: A different (extended) question; shows that analogues can fail. Says nothing about the classical equation.
events.remains: The classical problem, unaffected.
events.direction: Counterexample to an extended analogue; not the classical question.

events.what_happened: Oleg Karpenkov and Matty van Son, 'Generalised Markov numbers', arXiv 1809.01688 (5 Sep 2018). Constructs a counterexample to a generalised Markov uniqueness conjecture. Opened the arXiv abstract page.
events.delivers: A counterexample to a generalised (different) uniqueness conjecture; the abstract does not name the family. Says nothing about the classical equation.
events.remains: The classical problem, unaffected.

events.what_happened: Michelle Rabideau and Ralf Schiffler, 'Continued fractions and orderings on the Markov numbers', arXiv 1801.07155 (22 Jan 2018; v2 19 May 2020), Advances in Mathematics 370 (2020). Proves two of Aigner's ordering conjectures (fixed-numerator case), using continuant polynomials. Says nothing about the uniqueness claim itself. Opened the arXiv abstract page.
events.delivers: Ordering conjectures of Aigner (fixed-numerator case). Not uniqueness.
events.remains: Uniqueness, entirely.
events.doubts: A 2021 comment (arXiv 2105.10916, DoYong Kwon) examines the validity of the proof of the fixed-numerator conjecture; I read only its abstract, which says it 'discusses the validity' and does not say the proof fails.

events.what_happened: Kyungyong Lee, Li Li, Michelle Rabideau, Ralf Schiffler, 'On the ordering of the Markov numbers', arXiv 2010.13010 (25 Oct 2020; v2 11 Oct 2022), published Advances in Applied Mathematics 143 (2023). Gives a partial answer to an ordering question that 'would solve the uniqueness conjecture': the greater-x-coordinate lattice point gives the larger Markov number when the connecting slope is at least -8/7, and the smaller when it is at most -5/4; slopes 0 and 1 give two Aigner conjectures. Opened the arXiv abstract page.
events.delivers: Partial answer to an ordering question on lattice points (slope ranges -8/7 and -5/4 and the slopes 0 and 1); the authors say a complete answer would solve the uniqueness conjecture. So a partial result on a question that implies uniqueness, not uniqueness.
events.remains: Uniqueness, and the ordering question outside the stated slope ranges.

checked_by.who: Advances in Applied Mathematics (journal of record, per the search summary; I did not open the journal page)

events.what_happened: David Fisac, 'Markov's Conjecture on integral necklaces', arXiv 2501.15550 (v1 26 Jan 2025; v2 20 Feb 2025; v3 11 Aug 2025), math.GT. Starts from the geometric form of the uniqueness conjecture (simple length spectrum of the modular torus) and rewrites it combinatorially, as the injectivity of a function Phi on primitive necklaces; the abstract calls this a rewrite, not a proof. Opened the arXiv abstract page (v2); the statement that the conjecture is equivalent to injectivity of Phi is from a search summary of the HTML v1, not from text I read.
events.revisions: v1 26 Jan 2025 (differs from later versions in the power of 3 in Phi and in whether the trivial necklace is included); v2 20 Feb 2025; v3 11 Aug 2025.
events.delivers: Reformulation: the classical uniqueness conjecture is equivalent to injectivity of Phi on the set of necklaces (per the search summary of Theorem I.1). Establishes no uniqueness and no injectivity.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: the reformulated injectivity statement is unproved.

events.what_happened: Robert A. Gore, 'Patterns Within the Markov Tree', arXiv 2506.04299 (v1 4 Jun 2025; v2 26 Aug 2025, comment 'Updated Section 2'), math.GM, 23 pages. Derives generating and sequence functions for triplets in each region of the Markov tree, obtains a Pell equation for region numbers along the edges of all regions, and says that 'analysis of this Pell equation leads to the resolution of the Uniqueness Conjecture.' Section 2 is headed 'A Proof of The Uniqueness Conjecture'. Opened the arXiv abstract page, the arXiv PDF (compressed, unreadable) and the arXiv HTML v2 and v1 renderings.
events.revisions: v1 4 Jun 2025: Section 2 closes with 'Thus, the Uniqueness Conjecture is true'; abstract says 'resolution'. v2 26 Aug 2025: 'Updated Section 2'. In v2 the section still states the conjecture is true in its penultimate sentence, but its closing sentences say: 'The Uniqueness Conjecture is fundamentally an observation of a particular pattern within the Markov tree.' I did not diff the two versions' Section 2 text in full.
events.delivers: Claimed: that the region number of a Markov triplet determines the remaining values of that triplet, which the paper identifies with the Frobenius uniqueness conjecture. This is a claimed full resolution of the classical statement, expressed in region-number language; the paper does not restate it as a formal theorem and I have not checked that its region-number formulation is equivalent to the bullet's normalized-solution formulation.
events.remains: None, if the claim is correct. The argument's key steps are asserted in the text I read ('one can prove' that the baseline solution generates all solutions; 'to verify this, expand' with no expansion shown); the paper treats its Mathematica tables as illustrative, not as the basis of the argument.
events.doubts: (1) Single author, with no affiliation on the arXiv page, posting in math.GM. (2) The proof section is only partly written out: the Pell verification and the claim that the baseline solution generates all solutions are asserted, and the cases n = 0 and n = -1 are handled briefly. (3) The paper's own closing sentence calls the result 'an observation'. (4) The only reference is the Quanta article of 12 Dec 2023 (Kramer); it does not cite Frobenius, Aigner's book, Baragar, Button, Riedel or Zhang, although the conjecture's literature is long. (5) I found no review, comment, citing paper or retraction in any search. (6) The Sarnak 2015 remark in an OEIS comment (second-hand) says all claimed proofs have proved false.
events.direction: Claims uniqueness: cuts in the direction of the conjecture as stated.

events.what_happened: Tianyi Tao (Fudan University) and Bohan Yang (Shanghai Institute for Mathematics and Interdisciplinary Sciences), 'Markov's equation is not partition regular', arXiv 2510.10151 (v1 11 Oct 2025, the only version). Proves that the equation x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 3xyz is not partition regular over N, by a 9-colouring of N with no non-trivial monochromatic solution (Theorem 2.2), and notes that if the Uniqueness Conjecture holds, the equation is not partition regular (Proposition 1.5). Opened the arXiv HTML v1 rendering and the abstract page. Note: Tianyi Tao is not Terence Tao; a search summary mixed them up.
events.delivers: Unconditional: Markov's equation is not partition regular over N. Conditional direction: uniqueness would imply non-partition-regularity (Proposition 1.5), so the unconditional result is consistent with uniqueness and supports it only as a necessary-condition check. It does not prove uniqueness and does not use it.
events.remains: All of problem_asks. The paper says the conjecture 'remains unresolved in its full generality'.
events.directly_checkable: The 9-colouring of N in Theorem 2.2 can be checked by hand against the equation. A search summary describes the classes as built from residues mod 5 and 5-adic valuation; I did not verify that against the paper's definitions.
events.direction: Does not bear on uniqueness directly; the result is consistent with the conjecture (a necessary-condition check).
events.object: An explicit 9-colouring of the positive integers (Theorem 2.2) with no non-trivial monochromatic solution of x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 3xyz. It is a colouring, not an object related to uniqueness; it shows the equation is not partition regular over N. Explicit.

events.what_happened: Zhichao Chen and Zelin Jia, 'Tropicalization and cluster asymptotic phenomenon of generalized Markov equations', arXiv 2511.03428 (v1 5 Nov 2025; v2 18 Nov 2025, typos). Constructs a deformed Fock-Goncharov tropicalization for generalised Markov equations and proposes a 'generalized Markov uniqueness conjecture' (Conj. 8.2 in the search summary). Opened the arXiv abstract page; the classical conjecture is not mentioned in the abstract.
events.delivers: Nothing toward the classical question. It proposes a generalised uniqueness conjecture for generalised Markov equations and a rationality conjecture; it proves neither.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, and the generalised conjecture is proposed, not proved.

events.what_happened: Esther Banaian, 'Orderings of k-Markov Numbers', arXiv 2512.04026 (v1 3 Dec 2025; v2 13 Apr 2026). For the k-Markov numbers (solutions of x^2 + y^2 + z^2 + k(xy+xz+yz) = (3+3k)xyz, introduced by Gyoda and Matsushita), classifies lines along which they are monotone, and shows they satisfy Aigner's conjectures. Opened the arXiv abstract page.
events.delivers: Aigner-type ordering results for the k-generalised equation; by the abstract, k = 0 recovers the classical numbers, but the paper's results are for the k-family. Not the classical uniqueness question.
events.remains: The classical uniqueness question, entirely.
events.direction: Neutral for the classical problem; a different (generalised) question.

events.what_happened: Yasuaki Gyoda and Shuhei Maruyama, 'Uniqueness theorem of generalized Markov numbers that are prime powers', arXiv 2312.07329 (v1 12 Dec 2023; v2 11 Jul 2024), later published in INTEGERS 26 (2026), article A91 (the PDF header gives acceptance 22 June 2026 and publication 29 July 2026; I did not open the journal PDF). Generalises Cohn triples to the k-equation x^2+y^2+z^2+k(yz+zx+xy)=(3+3k)xyz and proves uniqueness for k-generalised Markov numbers that are prime powers, with a criterion for b not in {1, k+2}: if x^2+kx+1 = 0 mod b has at most two solutions, uniqueness holds. Opened the arXiv abstract page.
events.revisions: v1 12 Dec 2023; v2 11 Jul 2024; journal publication INTEGERS 26 (2026) A91 (2026; not re-dated here because the first public argument is the 2023 preprint).
events.delivers: Uniqueness for k-generalised Markov numbers that are prime powers, with criteria. For k = 0 this recovers a classical prime-power case; the bullet's classical statement is not settled.
events.remains: The classical statement for all Markov numbers, and the k-generalised statement for other numbers.

checked_by.who: INTEGERS (journal of record, per the search summary)
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper (2026, per the PDF header in a search summary)

events.direction: Generalised; neutral for the classical problem.

events.what_happened: Esther Banaian and Min Huang, 'Orderings of Generalized k-Markov Numbers', arXiv 2604.17445 (19 Apr 2026). Classifies lines along which generalised k-Markov numbers are monotone; says the results 'give evidence that a k-version of Frobenius' uniqueness conjecture, which has been proposed by Gyoda and Maruyama, could be true.' Opened the arXiv abstract page.
events.delivers: Evidence for a k-generalised analogue; not a proof of any uniqueness statement, classical or generalised.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.direction: Evidence for a generalised analogue only; neutral for the classical problem.

events.what_happened: A. P. Veselov, 'Markov fractions and Cohn matrices', arXiv 2604.17401 (v1 19 Apr 2026; v2 28 Aug 2026). Shows that Springborn's Markov fractions equal the index of Aigner's Cohn matrices, with a concatenation rule on the Conway topograph. The abstract does not mention Frobenius's conjecture. Opened the arXiv abstract page.
events.delivers: Identifies two families of invariants attached to Markov numbers; says nothing about uniqueness.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.doubts: A third-party AI-generated review (themoonlight.io) summary of this paper, seen in search results, said that the Frobenius uniqueness claim 'remains to be proved'; the abstract I read does not say so.

events.what_happened: Yasuaki Gyoda, 'An Introduction to the Lagrange and Markov Spectra through the Lens of Generalized Markov Numbers', arXiv 2609.28097 (v1 23 Sep 2026). An expository survey; the abstract says it covers 'generalizations of Frobenius's uniqueness conjecture' but does not say whether the classical conjecture is open. Opened the arXiv abstract page only, not the body.
events.delivers: Exposition, including generalisations of the uniqueness conjecture; no new uniqueness result stated in the abstract.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, as far as the abstract shows.

events.what_happened: Cormac O'Sullivan, 'Patterns in the Markov numbers and their generalizations', arXiv 2609.14149 (v1 12 Sep 2026; one version), 49 pages, math.NT and math.GT. Studies real solutions of x^2 + y^2 + z^2 - xyz = D for all real D (D = 0 is the Markov case), with an encoding function that is convex for D < 4, linear for D = 4 and concave for D > 4, and says the results generalise 'uniqueness conditions' to all D. The introduction, in the HTML rendering I read (truncated after 100,000 characters), states the uniqueness conjecture as 'the largest number in any triple on the Markov tree (3,15,6) determines the other two' and calls it a conjecture; Section 10 finds trees with labels in a quadratic field that have uniqueness. I did not find a citation to Gore, Tao-Yang or Riedel in the visible text.
events.delivers: Abstract: uniqueness conditions for the D-generalised encoding, including possibly D = 0. I could not establish from what I read whether the D = 0 specialisation of its uniqueness criterion settles the classical statement, or whether it is a criterion only in the generalised setting.
events.remains: Not established by my reading; the classical statement is presented in the introduction as open.
events.direction: Unclear; the introduction treats the classical question as open. Whether the paper's uniqueness conditions reach D = 0 is the open point for this entry.

disputes.summary: The classical claim has a repeated history of disputed or withdrawn proofs: Rosenberger 1976 (reported faulty, not opened), Zhou 2000 (withdrawn for an error in the proof), Riedel 2007 (withdrawn 2013) and Riedel 2012 (claimed, unrefereed; the 2007-2009 HAL review of the 2007 version found deficiencies), and Gore 2025 (claimed, unrefereed). Second-hand: an OEIS comment by Jonathan Sondow (1 May 2015) reports Sarnak as saying all claimed proofs have turned out false; I did not verify this against Sarnak or a primary source.

Riedel's 2012 preprint (arXiv 1208.4032) and Gore's 2025 preprint (arXiv 2506.04299) each claim the same classical resolution, 13 years apart and with no visible connection; neither has a reviewer on record in my searches. Gore's paper does not cite Riedel (its only reference is the Quanta article), so the two claims are not in dispute with each other in the sources, only with the literature's history.

summary: After the window (26 January 2024) I found one claimed resolution of the classical conjecture, Gore's 'Patterns Within the Markov Tree' (arXiv 2506.04299, June 2025, v2 August 2025), which states that a Pell-equation analysis resolves the Uniqueness Conjecture. It is a single-author preprint with no affiliation on arXiv; its Section 2 proof is only partly written (key steps asserted, 'one can prove'), and its closing sentence calls the result 'an observation'. I found no review, comment, citing paper or retraction of it in any search, so the honest status is claimed, unchecked. Its only reference is the Quanta 2023 article; it does not cite Frobenius, Aigner, Baragar, Button or Riedel. The only other in-window items that bear on the classical statement are: Tao and Yang (arXiv 2510.10151, Oct 2025), which proves Markov's equation is not partition regular and notes that uniqueness would imply that, a consistency check rather than evidence for uniqueness; Fisac (arXiv 2501.15550, Jan 2025), an equivalent reformulation as injectivity of a function on necklaces; and O'Sullivan (arXiv 2609.14149, Sept 2026), whose introduction treats the classical uniqueness as an open conjecture, though its generalised uniqueness conditions for all D might reach D = 0 and I could not read that section. The rest (Chen and Jia 2025, Banaian 2025 and Banaian and Huang 2026, Gyoda and Maruyama's 2023 preprint published in INTEGERS 2026, Veselov 2026, Gyoda's 2026 survey) treat generalised equations or neighbouring ordering questions and do not settle the classical statement. On the pre-window side, the record is of partial results (Button 2001; Lang and Tan 2005; Zhang 2006 twice; Baragar 1996; Lee, Li, Rabideau and Schiffler 2020) and of withdrawn or disputed claims (Zhou 2000; Riedel 2007 withdrawn; Riedel 2012, which I could not read in full and whose versions may differ). Close calls: (a) whether Gore's region-number formulation is equivalent to the bullet's normalized-solution formulation, which I did not check; (b) whether O'Sullivan's uniqueness criteria for general D specialise to D = 0 with a classical resolution; (c) whether Riedel's 2012 text, read in an ar5iv rendering of unknown version, still contains its admitted gaps in v12. AI involvement: I searched explicitly for AI involvement in the classical problem (GPT, Gemini, Claude, AlphaEvolve, AlphaProof, Axiom, Harmonic, OpenAI for Science, DeepMind, Erdos AI trackers, Lean formalisations, AI-assisted acknowledgements) and found no AI system credited with any Markov-uniqueness result. Every in-window source I opened names no AI system in its acknowledgements or statements; Gore and the Tao–Yang preprint credit no tools, and Gore's computations are Mathematica, which is computer algebra, not AI. Neighbouring 'Markov' AI results (Erdos problem 1196 on primitive sets via a Markov chain argument, and others from the 2026 AI-tracker coverage) concern different objects and are not in this record's events.
competing_reading: Gore's paper could be read as a genuine resolution: its Pell equation for region numbers is a clean idea, the arithmetic it uses is elementary, and an unrefereed single-author preprint should not be dismissed for lacking an affiliation. The counter is that the proof's key uniqueness step is asserted rather than shown, the paper's own closing sentence downgrades the result to 'an observation', and the conjecture has a long record of claimed proofs that did not survive. On the other side of Tao–Yang, the unconditional non-partition-regularity result can be read as a support for uniqueness, or as irrelevant to it, since it is a necessary-condition check and does not use uniqueness. Riedel 2012 could be read as a live candidate (its v12 is from August 2022, after the 2007 withdrawal and the review), but the admitted gaps in the 2012-era rendering point the other way.
what_would_settle_it: (1) A referee report, journal decision or expert note on Gore's Section 2, showing either that the Pell step is verified or that it fails; a citing paper treating Gore's argument. (2) The full text of Riedel's 1208.4032 v12 and its journal status, and the HAL review hal-00406601 with its authors and date. (3) The D = 0 specialisation in O'Sullivan's uniqueness criteria, with the statement of the theorem. (4) A primary source for Sarnak's 2015 statement and for Rosenberger's 1976 paper. (5) A search of MathSciNet and zbMATH for citations of Gore 2025 and Tao–Yang 2025, which I could not run.

events.credibility_reason: Withdrawn by the author in v2 for an error in the proof.
Reported as faulty by second-hand sources; the conjecture is universally still described as open; no primary source opened, so no specific error can be named.
Withdrawn by the author in 2013; a review reported deficiencies.

Twelve versions over ten years, unrefereed, withdrawn precursor with reported deficiencies, and a rendering in which the author concedes the framework cannot settle uniqueness; literature still calls the problem open.

Several F10 signals together: single unaffiliated author posting in math.GM on a century-old landmark problem; no engagement of any kind after 16 months; a 2026 paper by a specialist (O'Sullivan) still presents the conjecture as open; key steps asserted rather than proved; v2 revision softens the conclusion to 'an observation'; cites none of the field's literature; long history of failed claimed proofs.

judgement.why: The only post-snapshot event claiming to settle the statement is Gore 2025; it is answered whole/unreviewed but not_credible because many F10 signals coincide (unaffiliated math.GM author on a landmark problem, 16 months of silence, a 2026 specialist paper still calling the conjecture open, asserted key steps, a revision softening the claim to 'an observation', no engagement with the literature, a history of failed proofs). The close alternative was doubtful, which would have made the problem 'claimed'; the convergence of signals decided it. Tao-Yang proves a necessary consequence of uniqueness (non-partition-regularity), which settles no restriction of the statement, so none; its colouring is not an object bearing on uniqueness. Fisac is a reformulation (none); Chen-Jia, Banaian, O'Sullivan and Gyoda-Maruyama treat generalised equations (variant); Gyoda-Maruyama's journal publication is a 2026 revision of a 2023 preprint and stays pre-snapshot. Pre-snapshot partial results by Baragar, Button, Lang-Tan and Zhang are cases; pre-snapshot full claims are withdrawn (Zhou, Riedel 2007) or doubtful (Rosenberger, Riedel 2012), so none tiers resolved. No AI involvement anywhere.
judgement.doubts: O'Sullivan 2026 was read only to 100,000 of 234,005 characters; whether its uniqueness conditions specialise to D = 0 and settle a classical case is unknown — answered variant on the introduction calling the classical question open. Gore's region-number formulation was not checked for equivalence with the statement.
